claims.statement: The extension is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension built with WXT, React 19 and TypeScript that renders summaries as OpenUI Lang programs through the OpenUI Renderer.
There is no backend: the extension builds an AI SDK provider from the user's own credentials and streams completions directly from the extension page, so every model call is BYOK.

A single Appearance object (accent pen, marker highlighter, corner style, reading font) is resolved into CSS variables for the app chrome, OpenUI ThemeProvider tokens for the generated UI, chart palettes and Pele diagram colors, so the same tokens drive all four surfaces.

The background service worker only routes: it never renders or summarizes, but owns context-menu sync, the toolbar action popup vs side-panel mode, the per-tab side-panel lifecycle, and the choice of surface for a trigger.
The full-page app tab and the per-tab side panel mount the same React result view; App takes a surface prop ('page' | 'panel') and the sidepanel entrypoint renders App with surface="panel".

The app library extends openuiChatLibrary with the custom components SummaryHero, KeyNumbers/KeyNumber, Takeaways/Takeaway, Timeline/TimelineEvent, SourceQuote and Diagram plus the custom actions HighlightInPage and CopyText, with Card as the program root.

lib/openui.ts owns the system prompts (visual-first, chart-selection, diagram, length, layout and per-source-kind rules), the inline-mode prose/code split, parser validation, Mermaid validation, the repair message and edit-mode merging via mergeStatements.
The prompt's layout rule is chosen by the display setting (tab vs sidepanel), so the generated UI is shaped for the surface it will be shown in.

Only CSV sources enable the Query tools and $state bindings in the prompt, and the corresponding toolProvider executes csv_rows and csv_group in the browser, so filtering and grouping never call the model again.

lib/generate.ts runs the turn: it streams the completion, splits prose from code, and if the program is invalid it sends the error list back to the model exactly once, accepting the repair only when it does not leave more errors than before.

Validation covers both the OpenUI Lang program (parser errors, missing root, unresolved references) and every Diagram node, which is rendered with Pele so Mermaid errors are reported to the model too.

Refinement turns use OpenUI edit mode, where the model returns only changed statements that are merged into the current program, while follow-up questions use inline mode and may answer with plain prose or a compact UI.

The OpenUI Renderer does not execute custom actions: it emits an event that the app handles, which is how @HighlightInPage, @CopyText, URL opening and follow-up questions are fulfilled in SessionView.

Source extraction converts web pages to Markdown with Readability and Turndown (GFM keeps tables for charts), PDFs with pdf.js, CSV with Papa Parse into a dataset, and truncates content to the configured maxChars before it reaches the model.

History is persisted with the OpenUI Message Protocol (buildMessage / parseMessage) so form and $state values survive a reopen, and only the plain content is ever sent back to the model; at most 20 sessions are kept.

Persistent state lives in chrome.storage.local (settings with per-provider API keys, history, cached model lists) while pending requests and side-panel bookkeeping live in chrome.storage.session and are dropped after 10 minutes.
Settings are stored under the local: prefix rather than sync:, so API keys are never synchronized through the user's browser account.

browser.sidePanel.open() only works during a user gesture, so the display mode is encoded in the context-menu id instead of being read from storage at click time, and openSidePanelForTab is deliberately not async.

Every request is checked against the provider configuration before it runs: configProblem rejects a missing base URL, a missing API key for key-requiring providers, or an empty model, and the UI offers a link to Settings.

Local providers are supported without extra configuration because a declarativeNetRequest session rule rewrites the Origin header of the extension's own requests to localhost, so Ollama does not need OLLAMA_ORIGINS.
Model output is treated as untrusted: Pele rendering disables links and images, and a diagram failure is displayed as text rather than markup.

wxt.config.ts declares the runtime permissions (storage, sidePanel, activeTab, scripting, contextMenus, unlimitedStorage, declarativeNetRequest, favicon, clipboardWrite), optional_host_permissions for the provider API domain, the localized name/description, and the Alt+Shift+S _execute_action command.

UI localization is bundled at build time from locales/<lang>/<namespace>.json, with English as the source of truth whose keys are type-checked through an i18next module augmentation, so a missing English key breaks the type check.

Operationally the project is driven by pnpm scripts: dev for the loaded extension with hot reload, compile for type-checking, build for .output/chrome-mv3, and check:i18n to validate the locale folders against English.

The manifest is not fully described by wxt.config.ts: WXT derives the rest from the entrypoint folders and public/, so the built .output/chrome-mv3/manifest.json adds the background service worker, action.default_popup (popup.html), side_panel.default_path (sidepanel.html), options_ui (options.html, open_in_tab) and the icon set.

A pending summarize request is consumed exactly once: takeRequest removes it from chrome.storage.session when the result view picks it up, so reloading the result page does not re-run the summary, and a missing request surfaces as an expired-request error; the per-tab side-panel pointer is ignored after 60 seconds.

useSession owns the whole session lifecycle: each turn aborts the previous AbortController and moves through the phases idle, extracting, summarizing, refining and answering, the session is committed and persisted after each turn, and reopening a session that has a source but no summary triggers a fresh summary run.
